text:
alex: Quick question — external on-call (vendor) needs access to the runbook + ability to view LLM traces for incident debugging. We must not expose raw user logs or PII. What's the least-privilege console role combo we can give? Prefer ephemeral/JIT access. cc @maria @jen

maria: For vendors I'd avoid broad logging roles. Recommend a JIT flow + a custom role that grants: runbook read, llm_traces.read (redacted), and no BigQuery / raw log sinks. :lock:

jen: Agreed. Do NOT grant `roles/logging.viewer` or project-wide `Viewer`. If we need console access to the runbook UI, `roles/runbook.viewer` (if available) or `roles/browser` + custom trace role is safer.

leo: We already built a redacted-trace role for audits. Vendor pattern: create `customRoles/redactedLlMTraceViewer` + ephemeral binding. Example binding we used before:
```
bindings:
- role: projects/PROJECT_ID/customRoles/redactedLlMTraceViewer
  members:
  - user:vendor+oncall@example.com
```
This role only surfaces tokenized user ids and strips request payloads.

security-bot: Policy reminder: external vendors require a signed DPA + security addendum and max 90-day JIT window. Any permanent grants will trigger a review. :warning:

alex: Good call. Can someone create the custom role and open a JIT request? I'll approve once the runbook entry is linked and the DPA is on file.

maria: I'll create the role and submit the JIT ticket now. Will explicitly exclude BigQuery dataset access and logging sinks. ETA ~2h.

jen: Also add a short runbook note for engineers: use `redact_traces --level pii` before sharing. Example CLI: `redact_traces --project redwood-prod --level pii`.

alex: Perfect — please @me on the JIT ticket when it's ready. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
